summary.text: A 22-year-old African American female with a history of hypertension and iron deficiency anemia presented with generalized fatigue and new onset dyspnea on exertion of three-week duration. She had heavy menstrual bleeding requiring blood transfusions in the last six months and a transfusion of four units of packed red blood cells one month ago. Home medications included iron supplements and oral contraceptive pills. On admission her heart rate was 132 beats/minute, with pale conjunctiva, icteric sclera and morbid obesity.

Laboratory review showed hemoglobin 4.8 g/dL, hematocrit 13.4%, platelets 91,000, haptoglobin 2 mg/dL, LDH 1868 IU/L and elevated total bilirubin 1.5 mg/dL, with marked anisocytosis and few schistocytes on the peripheral smear. No alloantibodies were detected and the direct antiglobin (Coombs) test with IgG was positive, suggestive of AIHA. Vitamin B12 was 60 pg/mL with elevated homocysteine and methylmalonic acid, and intrinsic factor blocking and anti-parietal cell antibodies were present, resulting in pernicious anemia.

After receiving two units of PRBCs for symptomatic anemia, she was started on prednisone 100 mg daily for the treatment of AIHA, with daily parenteral vitamin B12 supplementation along with iron and folic acid supplementation. Over a course of five days of treatment hemoglobin and hematocrit improved to 7.1 g/dL and 20.9% with a good reticulocyte response of 345,000. Steroids were then decreased to prednisone 40 mg and she was discharged home.

Outpatient upper GI endoscopy showed a patchy area of nonerosive gastritis in the antrum and atrophic mucosa in the body of the stomach; biopsy revealed chronic active atrophic gastritis with intestinal metaplasia and negative Helicobacter pylori immunostaining. At clinic visits prednisone 40 mg daily and monthly subcutaneous vitamin B12 were continued. After the direct Coombs test became negative at six months, steroids were tapered off over two months. Two years after initial presentation hemoglobin was 12.4 g/dL and hematocrit 38%.
